title: Patient Financial Account Terms — Late Fees Posted After the Final Notice on Pre-Placement Statements
content:
**Term.** On the Patient Financial Account, the most recently posted late fee, when it was posted after the account's final notice date, is left off the pre-placement statement for an account charged no more than two late fees in the 12 calendar months before the handling date:

- in full, when the account was opened at least 60 calendar months before the handling date;
- 50 percent of it, when the account was opened more recently.

For an account charged more late fees in those 12 months, the late fee is shown.

**Calendar-month windows.** A window of calendar months for the pre-placement statement ends on the handling date and reaches back that many months, a date on the same calendar day that many months earlier falling outside it. An account opened on the same calendar day 60 months before the handling date was therefore opened at least 60 months before it; a late fee dated on the same calendar day 12 months earlier is outside the 12 months.

## Terms at a glance

| Late fee posted last was posted after the final notice date | Late fees charged in the 12 months | Account opened | Left off |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | 2 or fewer | 60 or more months ago | the whole late fee |
| yes | 2 or fewer | fewer than 60 months ago | 50 percent of the late fee |
| yes | 3 or more | any | nothing; the fee is shown |
| no, or no late fee | any | any | nothing |

The count of late fees includes the late fee posted last. The final notice date and the opening date are those recorded on the account.

**Hypothetical example.** A final notice dated 1 May; a late fee of 10.00 posted on 20 May; one other late fee in the preceding 12 months (two in all); account opened 38 months before the handling date: 5.00 is left off. The same account opened 72 months before: 10.00 is left off.
